summary: A city phases in a higher minimum wage and a year later studies find prices barely moved while hours for the lowest paid slipped.
realLife: Seattle's $15 wage law began phasing in April 1, 2015. University of Washington researchers found in April 2016 little or no price increase relative to nearby areas, and in July 2016 that the lowest-paid workers' hours fell by about an hour a week on average, with pay gains mostly tied to a strong regional economy.
sources: University of Washington News, Seattle $15 wage law prices one year later, Apr 18, 2016: https://www.washington.edu/news/2016/04/18/early-analysis-of-seattles-15-wage-law-effect-on-prices-minimal-one-year-after-implementation/

University of Washington News, Seattle minimum wage effects modest, Jul 25, 2016: https://www.washington.edu/news/2016/07/25/minimum-wage-study-effects-of-seattle-wage-hike-modest-may-be-overshadowed-by-strong-economy/
